x_omi_reference.note: Mechanical projection of the OMI contract. OMI's reference doc is the semantic authority; on conflict, fix this schema, never OMI.

exists.description: Optional existing-asset binding: this entity is already in the target app, so its attributes are the shape to VERIFY, not to create. Valid only under target_mode 'existing-app'. Absent means create (the default). An attribute of an `exists: true` entity may carry `create: true`: the attribute is to be ADDED to the existing entity, with its declared data_type; every other attribute stays a shape to verify. `create` on an entity without `exists` is an error - a created entity creates all of its attributes.

data_type.description: CLOSED VOCABULARY, ONE REGISTER. An open string here is unvalidatable and the failure it hides is a certain publish failure, not a style slip: the model API accepts any string as an entity-attribute DataType, validation checks shape rather than membership in the platform's closed enum, and the enum is only enforced by the publish-time migration-script generator (OS-RDBS-GEN-40002, masked as OS-DPL-50203). Three admitted forms. (1) A basic type, in the ODC literal register - the twelve names above, as the platform docs spell them. This file is a projection whose semantic authority is outsystems-mentor-implementation, whose contract states the literal DataType string ('For an ordinary auto-number primary key, state the literal DataType string Long Integer'), and the string is rendered verbatim into the Mentor prompt. (2) A Text with its length, Text(200) - odc-studio-language-elements.md requires stating it, because an unstated length silently chooses 50 and truncates. (3) The relationship form '<TargetEntity> Identifier', single-token entity name, which by construction has no camelCase spelling. NOT members: the legacy camelCase register (text, longInteger, dateTime) and the three legacy identifier tokens (integerIdentifier, longIntegerIdentifier, platformDefaultIdentifier), all admitted between 2026-08-27 and 2026-09-01 and now refused with a message naming the canonical replacement - the identifier tokens all mean an auto-number primary key and canonicalise to 'Long Integer', never to a case-split of themselves; the seven App Generator VirtualTypeKind values with no ODC basic type (url, percentage, rating, imageUrl, multiLineText, foreignKey, and foreignKey's spec-level kin); and near-miss spellings such as DateTime for Date Time, which are read as a Text attribute named after a type. The bare strings 'Identifier', 'Integer Identifier', 'Long Integer Identifier' and 'Text Identifier' have the shape of form (3) but are rejected by the validator: all four validate cleanly and then fail every publish.

enum_values.description: Required on every attribute. null on a plain attribute; on a foreign key pointing at a static entity, the ordered list of that entity's record names, which seeds the target when it has no entities[] entry of its own.

create.description: See the entity-level `exists` description: valid only on an attribute of an `exists: true` entity, where it means this attribute is to be ADDED rather than verified.

name.description: The ODC ELEMENT name of the screen - what the built model's node carries as `Name` - not the human title. This artifact requires letters, digits and underscore only, first character a letter - a contract of this schema, deliberately a safe subset of the naming vocabulary ODC publishes for the names it derives itself, since no screen-element grammar is published: `A4PrintPreview`, never `A4 Print Preview`. Every downstream consumer matches this string against the model exactly (outsystems-mentor-implementation/scripts/recompute_assertions.py `_screen_id`, and the render-gate spec this validator emits), so a display name here reports the screen as absent from a build that contains it. Measured 2026-09-02 on restaurant-app-v3: 6 of 7 screens SCREEN_MISSING for this reason alone. Put the human title in `display_name`.

display_name.description: Optional. The human title of the screen, free-form and translatable - `A4 Print Preview`. Carried for the reader and for copy; no consumer matches it against the model. Omit it when the element name already reads as the title.

render_gate.description: Optional, and the ONE gate-bearing channel for a runtime claim. Each entry is a named assertion a render gate can execute, or an explicit declaration that no assertion is derivable. This is where a disclosure about what the screen must SHOW stops being prose: the acceptance_checklist stays advisory by design, so a claim that must be checked belongs here, exactly as an enforced count belongs in the screen's `assertions` object. SKILL-LOCAL EXTENSION, added 2026-08-30: the OMI contract this file projects does not carry this key and ignores it, exactly as it ignores `assertions`. It is per-screen and optional so the divergence stays bounded - the top-level `required` list is untouched, and a blueprint without it is the same artifact it was before. Cross-field rules the shape cannot express are in scripts/validate_blueprint.py.

label.description: Names the gate row. Unique across the blueprint, because a disclosure references it by this name alone.

assert.description: widget: the element is present. populated: it carries some value. text: it displays THIS content - the only one that can fail on a placeholder, since a placeholder is not empty. known-unverified: no assertion is derivable and the reason is stated rather than left unsaid.

selector.description: CSS. Required on widget/populated/text; forbidden on known-unverified. An empty string is the honest 'no confident selector' - the gate records that screenshot-only.

contains.description: text only, exclusive with equals: a fragment the displayed text must carry. Case-insensitive at the gate.

equals.description: text only, exclusive with contains: the exact displayed text. Case-sensitive at the gate.

reason.description: known-unverified only: why no assertion is derivable. Must name a token the blueprint already declares - a requirement id, a screen, a region or an entity - so a coverage hole is stated in terms of what it leaves uncovered.

discharges.description: Requirement ids this entry answers (BR-SC-006, UC-005). The link a reviewer follows from a cited requirement to the check that covers it.

reuse.description: Optional existing-asset binding: this region IS an app-local block the target app already has. `block` names the asset and may be flow-qualified ('MainFlow/RecentQueriesPanel'), unlike the bare catalog token in outsystems_hints.block. Satisfies the Block Mapping Gate on its own and must not coexist with outsystems_hints.block or custom_block_needed. Valid only under target_mode 'existing-app'.

items.description: Children of a group region. Each item is itself a region and may carry the same optional `reuse` binding as a direct main_content entry; the validator applies every reuse rule at both levels.

reuse.description: Same existing-asset binding as at the top level, for a region nested inside a group.

acceptance_checklist.description: Advisory, human-facing prose only. NOT authoritative: main_content is the source of truth. Any count that must be enforced belongs in a screen's optional `assertions` object, which the validator recomputes from main_content.
